newsitem.title: USA: Cat returns home safely from apparent abduction.
newsitem.headline: Cat returns home safely from apparent abduction.

text.p: Tipper the cat, who dialed the emergency telephone number 911 to save his life last summer, arrived home unscathed after what his owners believed was a kidnapping ordeal, a spokeswoman for the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Department said on Friday.

The 6-month-old gray-and-white kitten arrived at his home at the Flying Cloud Mobile Home Park on Thursday afternoon, where he lived with his owner, Gail Curtis. Tipper had disappeared on Tuesday after he was left tethered outdoors.

The cat became famous on July 8 when he saved himself from choking on his flea collar by going to Curtis's telephone and hitting the speed dial button that reached the "911" emergency operator. The dispatcher heard the kitten's anguished cries and sent an emergency crew, which rescued him.
Tipper became international news and police got telephone calls from as far away as Britain, Australia and India.
But his owners had feared this week that even Tipper would not be able to outwit his "catnappers."

Police said they did not know what had happened to Tipper. They added they could not confirm a report in Friday's Tampa Tribune that a mysterious green pickup truck had driven into the trailer park and let Tipper out.
